article.title: NFL EDGE Monday Morning Brief
article.dek: One game closes Week 6: the 5-0 49ers host Jayden Daniels and the Commanders tonight. Here's the news, the one line left, and how to use the app on it.

items.headline: One game left: Commanders at 49ers, tonight 8:15 p.m. ET
paragraphs: Monday Night Football closes Week 6: the Washington Commanders (1-3-1) visit the unbeaten San Francisco 49ers (5-0) at Levi's Stadium, 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN/ABC.
San Francisco has yet to lose, and Brock Purdy is playing like an early MVP candidate. Washington gets Jayden Daniels back from injury and is coming off a 27-27 tie with the Giants.
Both DraftKings and FanDuel are dealing San Francisco -7.5 with a 51.5 total. The app's QB board confirms Daniels and Purdy as the expected starters.
items.takeaway: Tonight is the whole slate: run the app's process on this one before inactives post.

items.headline: Injury report, all in one place
paragraphs: Commanders: Jayden Daniels (left elbow) played last week and is expected to start. Marcus Mariota (MCL sprain) is out and didn't travel. Jacory Croskey-Merritt re-injured his groin, didn't practice all week, and was ruled out Friday. Rachaad White (shoulder) and Austin Ekeler (chest) are on the report. Stefon Diggs (hamstring) practiced Friday and could be active.
49ers: Deebo Samuel (hamstring) is out. Christian Kirk (calf) and Mike Evans (ribs) are questionable.
The app's quarterback board agrees with the reports: Daniels and Purdy are the expected starters, and it hasn't flagged any QB change.
items.takeaway: Biggest hit is Washington's backfield: the top rusher is out and the next two are banged up, so Daniels' legs carry more of the run game.

items.headline: Weather: fine football weather in Santa Clara
paragraphs: The National Weather Service forecast for Monday night is mostly cloudy, falling into the mid-40s, with a light south wind at 2 to 12 mph and gusts up to 20.
That's mild October football weather. Nothing here to worry about.
items.takeaway: Weather is a non-factor tonight; judge this game on the teams, not the sky.

items.headline: Inactives land about 90 minutes before kickoff
paragraphs: The final inactive lists post about 90 minutes before the 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff, around 6:45 p.m. ET.
This morning's brief can't have them yet. The questionable tags to watch: Washington's Stefon Diggs, and San Francisco's Christian Kirk and Mike Evans.
items.takeaway: That's tonight's one pending info event: check inactives before you lock anything in.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: No cards tonight: here's what that means
paragraphs: All three of the app's headline lanes are empty this morning: Hit Rate, Balanced, and Value all show no play. No offer on the board satisfied the frozen lane contracts.

Quick refresher on the cards. Hit Rate is the supported pick that looks most likely to win; it gives up value to chase win probability. Balanced is a strong pick without paying too much; the middle ground, and a fine starting point if you're newer to this. Value is always the model's +EV play.

With only Monday night left and the board sitting at San Francisco -7.5 with a 51.5 total, no lane cleared its bar. The app's honest answer tonight is no play at these prices. That's the filter working, not a broken board.
items.takeaway: No card is a verdict too: the model doesn't have to like anything every night.

items.headline: Your book's number isn't -7.5? Tap Check
paragraphs: The board refreshes every morning and evening, but your book is your book. If your number or price differs from what the app saw, tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and the evaluator.
What you get is a bet or no-bet verdict on your price. That's a full re-evaluation of the actual number in front of you, not a blind override of the board.
items.takeaway: Never bet the app's number at your book's worse number: Check your price first.

items.headline: Learn the Game: the vig
paragraphs: Hypothetical example, clearly labeled: imagine a coin-flip bet where both sides pay -110. You risk $1.10 to win $1.
To break even at -110, you don't need to win half your bets. You need to win about 52.4%. That gap, between 50% and 52.4%, is the vig: the book's cut for taking the bet.

That's why price matters as much as picking winners. A bet at -110 needs 52.4% to break even, but the same bet at -105 only needs about 51.2%. The team didn't change; the price did, and the math got easier.
items.takeaway: Every time you shop a better price or skip a bad one, you're paying less vig. That's free edge, and it compounds.

items.headline: Overnight: the total ticked down to 51.5
paragraphs: The only real movement overnight is on tonight's total. Last night DraftKings was dealing 52.5; this morning both DraftKings and FanDuel sit at 51.5.
The spread hasn't budged: San Francisco -7.5 on both books. DraftKings' juice shifted a touch (from -110 both ways last night to -108/-112), but the line itself is steady.
Every Sunday board is off now; those games played, so there's nothing left to move on them. All market discussion for today lives in this section.
items.takeaway: Total down a point at DK to meet 51.5; spread steady at -7.5. If your book still shows 52.5, Check your price before assuming the move.

items.headline: Monday game? Monday check
paragraphs: Tonight's order of operations. First, read the app's answer as it stands: no card at these prices is a real answer. Second, wait for inactives about 90 minutes before kickoff; that's the one pending event that can change the picture. Third, if your book still shows a good number after that and Check says bet, bet it. A good number tonight beats a hoped-for number that never comes.
And the occasional honesty nudge: settlement is manual, so the tracker only works if you're honest with yourself. Log the losers too.
items.takeaway: Check your price, wait for inactives, then trust the verdict. And write down every bet, win or lose.
